vt-sos-2026-state-general-list.agency: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division
vt-sos-2026-state-general-list.title: 2026 General Election Candidate Listing/Financial Disclosure (qualified candidates): statewide offices and the General Assembly
vt-sos-2026-state-general-list.note: Linked from the Candidates page (https://sos.vermont.gov/elections/election-info-resources/candidates/). Workbook read in memory, never saved; columns taken by name, only Contest, District Name, Name On Ballot, Party and Vote for Count. Town of residence, addresses, phones, e-mail, websites and financial disclosures never read. The list gives no ballot positions; its order, alphabetical by surname as 17 V.S.A. 2472(b)(2) prints the ballot, is stored as the ballot order. No status column, so a withdrawn candidate, no longer listed, cannot be counted. The Secretary's district codes are shown as the Legislature's district names. Other offices on the list: Representative To Congress (6), left to the federal pages; and the county offices and justices of the peace (2,300 rows), loaded as local races from the same workbook.

vt-sos-2026-state-primary-list.agency: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division
vt-sos-2026-state-primary-list.title: 2026 Primary Election Candidate Listing/Financial Disclosure (qualified candidates): statewide offices and the General Assembly
vt-sos-2026-state-primary-list.note: Who was printed on each party's August 11 primary ballot (the results' printed candidates must be exactly these) and the registered write-in candidates (21 for these offices; the registration names no party). The same five columns only, and the write-in sheet's office, district and name columns.

vt-sos-2026-state-primary-results.agency: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division
vt-sos-2026-state-primary-results.title: 2026 August Primary Election Results (official), statewide offices, State Senate and State Representative
vt-sos-2026-state-primary-results.note: Linked from the Elections Results & Data page (https://sos.vermont.gov/elections/election-info-resources/elections-results-data/); read from the files the results site's own page fetches (https://static.electionresults.vermont.gov/elections/...), marked official, 247/247 towns reporting. Every town's candidates, write-ins, blank votes and spoiled ballots add up to its total, and the towns to the district-wide and statewide rows. A field is a party primary with more candidates than seats; its total is the candidates' votes plus every write-in vote (blanks and spoiled ballots left out). Write-in names are shown only for a write-in who won the nomination, or a registered write-in candidate recorded in one party's primary for that office and district; every other write-in is counted in the total and never named (9 registered write-ins were recorded in more than one party's primary, so in neither is the name shown). The results' town table gives the counties each district reaches.

vt-sos-2026-state-primary-winners.agency: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division
vt-sos-2026-state-primary-winners.title: 2026 August Primary Winner Listing
vt-sos-2026-state-primary-winners.note: Control: every candidate's votes and winner mark agree with the results (393 party primaries compared). Workbook read in memory, never saved; Winner, Name on Ballot, Party, Office Name, District, Votes and Percent(%) only; addresses and phones never read. Its percentages are of all votes counted, blank votes included.

vt-sos-2026-state-primary-canvass.agency: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division
vt-sos-2026-state-primary-canvass.title: 2026 August Primary Official Canvass - Town by Town: the Official Report of the Canvassing Committee (17 V.S.A. 2368-2371)
vt-sos-2026-state-primary-canvass.note: Control for the six statewide offices: every candidate's votes, the write-in, overvote, blank and total figures and the starred winners equal the results site's statewide rows. Only the committee's report pages are read.

vt-openstates-roster.title: Sitting legislators and statewide officials
vt-openstates-roster.note: Who holds each seat today, and which candidates serve now. The roster does not carry the State Treasurer or the Auditor of Accounts.

vt-census-2024-county-codes.title: Cartographic boundary file, counties, 2024 (1:500,000)
vt-census-2024-county-codes.note: Five-digit county codes (GEOID) for Vermont's fourteen counties, named as the results' town table names them.

vt-sos-2026-local-general-list.agency: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division
vt-sos-2026-local-general-list.title: 2026 General Election Candidate Listing/Financial Disclosure (qualified candidates): county offices and justices of the peace
vt-sos-2026-local-general-list.note: The workbook the state races are read from, read in memory and never saved. Six columns are read, by their headings: Contest, District Name (the county or the town), Name On Ballot, Party, Vote for Count and Term Length(Years); only those cells of the county and town rows are kept on disk. Town of residence, addresses, phones, e-mail, websites and financial disclosures are never read. Of the workbook's 2,619 rows, 103 are for county offices and 2,197 for justices of the peace, each one candidate in one race; the other 319 are state and federal offices. The list states no ballot order and has no status column.

vt-sos-2026-local-results-election-list.agency: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division
vt-sos-2026-local-results-election-list.title: Vermont Election Results: the list of elections
vt-sos-2026-local-results-election-list.note: Read to find the November 3, 2026 general election and any other election a clerk has listed for the same day (1). Election dates, kinds and towns only; the file carries no contact details.

vt-sos-2026-local-november-index.agency: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division
vt-sos-2026-local-november-index.title: 2026 General Election (November 3, 2026) on the election results site: the election's index and town table
vt-sos-2026-local-november-index.note: The town table: each of the 247 towns and cities with its county, which is how a town's justices are filed under a county; 9 unorganized towns and gores are listed apart. No contact details in the file. The date given as published is the site's own last-updated stamp, on Vermont's clock.

vt-sos-2026-local-november-county-contes.agency: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division
vt-sos-2026-local-november-county-contes.title: 2026 General Election (November 3, 2026) on the election results site: county contests
vt-sos-2026-local-november-county-contes.note: Before any vote is counted the file already lists each county contest with the number to elect and the names and parties under it: 70 contests, 103 names. Read as a second route to the candidate list; only the office, county, number to elect, names and parties are kept, no vote. The site serves this file under a name that changes each time it is refreshed (as read: 68d61e96-1d28-4210-8c1d-8e90512ae105-cty-20261001002604.json, 857,077 bytes), found through the election's index, so the address given is the site's own page; the fingerprint is of the copy read.

vt-sos-2026-local-november-town-contests.agency: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division
vt-sos-2026-local-november-town-contests.title: 2026 General Election (November 3, 2026) on the election results site: town contests
vt-sos-2026-local-november-town-contests.note: Each town's justice of the peace contest with the number to elect and the names and parties under it: 247 contests, 2,197 names, 18 contests with no name. The 37 ballot questions in 16 towns are counted and their words never read. Only the office, town, number to elect, names and parties are kept, no vote. The site serves this file under a name that changes each time it is refreshed (as read: 68d61e96-1d28-4210-8c1d-8e90512ae105-t-20261001002604.json, 738,579 bytes), found through the election's index, so the address given is the site's own page; the fingerprint is of the copy read.

vt-census-2024-county-subdivisions.title: Cartographic boundary file, county subdivisions, Vermont, 2024 (1:500,000)
vt-census-2024-county-subdivisions.note: Names with their kind word (Addison town, Barre city) and five-digit codes of Vermont's towns and cities, read from the file's attribute table; no shapes are read. A town on the Secretary's lists is matched within its county by name (SAINT for St., and CITY or TOWN where two places share a name) and only when exactly one fits.

vt-sos-2026-local-town-election-04ff6132.agency: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division
vt-sos-2026-local-town-election-04ff6132.title: Another election listed for November 3, 2026 on the election results site: its index
vt-sos-2026-local-town-election-04ff6132.note: Read to see whether a town's own election on the same day has an office posted (the town, its county and the address of its town file only); nothing is posted yet.

vt-sos-2026-local-town-election-04ff6132.agency: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division
vt-sos-2026-local-town-election-04ff6132.title: Another election listed for November 3, 2026 on the election results site: its town file
vt-sos-2026-local-town-election-04ff6132.note: Only counted: how many contests for an office and how many questions it holds; nothing is posted yet. The site serves the file under a name that changes each time it is refreshed (as read: 04ff6132-3110-40bc-b52f-50e36fd2316b-t-20261001002238.json, 16 bytes), so the address given is the site's own page; the fingerprint is of the copy read.

local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 each of Vermont's 14 counties elects two assistant judges, a probate judge, a state's attorney and a sheriff for four years and a high bailiff for two, and every town and city elects its justices of the peace for two years; all are on the general election ballot with party names. Selectboards, town clerks and treasurers, listers, constables, city councils, mayors, village trustees and school boards are not on it: they are chosen at annual town, city, village and school district meetings, held on the first Tuesday of March in most places (March 3 this year) and in April or May in a few.
local_calendar.s: Vermont Constitution, chapter II, sections 43 and 50 to 52; 17 V.S.A. 2640 and 2646 and 16 V.S.A. 423 (annual meetings); the Secretary of State's list of 2026 elections on its results site; term lengths as the Secretary's candidate list gives them

local_coverage.t: Loaded from the Secretary of State's 2026 General Election Candidate Listing (updated 2026-09-23): 70 county contests in all 14 counties (assistant judge, probate judge, state's attorney, sheriff and high bailiff) with 103 candidates, and the justice of the peace contest of 247 towns and cities with 2,197 candidates; 18 of those contests have no candidate on the list and are shown with none. The contests, including the ones with no candidate, each town's county and the number to elect also come from the Secretary's election results site, which already lists the November 3 contests, and the two agree on every contest, name, party and number to elect. Left out: the 37 ballot questions in 16 towns; the 9 unorganized towns and gores, for which no justice of the peace contest is listed; and anything a town, city or school district decides at a meeting of its own. The list has no status column, so a candidate who withdrew is simply absent and cannot be counted, and it states no ballot order: the ballot prints each office's names alphabetically by surname, and names are shown here by surname.
local_coverage.s: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division: 2026 General Election Candidate Listing/Financial Disclosure and the 2026 General Election on the election results site; 17 V.S.A. 2472 (how the ballot lists names)

gaps.w: a town election set for the same day
gaps.r: The Secretary of State's results site lists a town election in Danby for November 3, 2026, apart from the general election; no office or question has been posted for it yet, so nothing can be shown and it cannot be said whether an office is being filled.

gaps.w: offices filled at a special town, city or school district meeting on November 3
gaps.r: A town, city, village or school district can warn a special meeting for November 3 to fill an office; those elections are run by the local clerk and are not on the Secretary of State's candidate list, so only the ones a clerk has entered on the Secretary's results site can be seen from here.
